headline: Anthropic files for IPO on Nasdaq under ticker 'ANT'
summary: The AI company's S-1 filing reveals massive compute deals and executive compensation, preparing for a public market debut.
details: Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, has officially filed its S-1 prospectus with the SEC, signaling its intent to go public on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol 'ANT'. This move positions Anthropic to potentially beat rival OpenAI to the public market.

The S-1 filing, made public after a confidential submission in June, offers a detailed look into the company's financial standing and future strategies. It disclosed an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of this year, though the majority of this is attributed to accounting charges related to funding notes.

Significant portions of the filing detail Anthropic's substantial commitments for computing power. The company plans to spend approximately $3.1 billion per month with SpaceX for Nvidia GPUs, totaling up to $120.5 billion by 2029. Further commitments include $44.9 billion with Microsoft, $114.5 billion with Google, and $110 billion with Amazon through 2033 or 2029.

Anthropic's vision, as outlined in the filing, emphasizes the transformative potential of AI to accelerate scientific innovation and economic growth. The company aims to manage the associated risks while pursuing these benefits.

The filing also sheds light on executive compensation. CEO Dario Amodei received nearly $18 million in 2025, primarily from stock and option awards. President and co-founder Daniela Amodei was the second-highest paid executive, earning $16.4 million in the same year.

The company plans to spend approximately $3.1 billion per month with SpaceX for Nvidia GPUs, totaling up to $120.5 billion by 2029. Further commitments include $44.9 billion with Microsoft, $114.5 billion with Google, and $110 billion with Amazon through 2033 or 2029.

Anthropic's vision, as outlined in the filing, emphasizes the transformative potential of AI to accelerate scientific innovation and economic growth. The company aims to manage the associated risks while pursuing these benefits.

The filing also sheds light on executive compensation. CEO Dario Amodei received nearly $18 million in 2025, primarily from stock and option awards. President and co-founder Daniela Amodei was the second-highest paid executive, earning $16.4 million in the same year.
